summary:
Etsy is laying off roughly 220 employees, about 12% of its workforce, as part of a restructuring the company says is intended to improve coordination and speed of decision-making, per a U.S. SEC filing. The cuts fall mostly on the product and engineering organization, according to CEO Kruti Patel Goyal in an email to staff.

Patel Goyal framed the move as structural rather than financial: cost savings are described as a consequence, not the objective, and she said the company did not begin with a cost reduction target or an aim to shrink Etsy. She added that Etsy will keep investing in the business and the team and will continue hiring in areas tied to long-term strategy.

She also stated the cuts were not driven by AI, while acknowledging that AI is changing how everyone works and will keep reshaping how Etsy builds products and solves problems. As tools evolve, she said, the skills needed, the ways teams work together, and the capabilities built across the company must evolve too.

Severance terms: at least 16 weeks of severance pay, with more based on tenure, plus continued healthcare support for up to 12 months and other benefits.

Separately, Etsy's audit committee approved a new stock repurchase program authorizing buybacks of up to an additional $2 billion of common stock, also disclosed in the SEC filing. Etsy reported quarterly results the same day after market close.

The piece is a Reuters wire report (reporting by Arriana McLymore, editing by Aurora Ellis) republished by Allwork.Space. It contains no discussion of workplace operations topics such as office attendance policy, desk booking, visitor management, or facilities practice.
